As a shadow, I follow my person everywhere they go. I start the day when they wake up, stretching across the floor as the morning light peeks through the curtains. They get out of bed, and I mimic their movements, rising and falling with each step.

In the bathroom, I watch as they brush their teeth and get ready. The mirror reflects both of us, but only they can see themselves. I'm just a dark outline, always present but never noticed. They eat breakfast, and I sit beside them, a silent companion.

At work, I'm there as they sit at their desk. I adjust with each movement, sometimes long and thin, other times short and wide. When they walk to meetings, I stride alongside, casting on the walls and floors. I notice how people step around me, not wanting to "step on" a shadow, even though they know it's just light and shadow.

During lunch, I'm under the table, hidden from view. But when they go outside, I become more visible. The sun is high, and I'm a clear silhouette. They might glance down and see me, but usually, they don't. I'm part of the background, a constant but unnoticed presence.
